hypothesis: Seeded from the historical corpus. Before any experiment of its own the agent believes campus content propagates through relatability and a moderately ironic register.

content.headline: HISTORICAL PRIOR
content.visual_description: Not a generated post. The centroid genome of 41,206 sampled campus-niche videos that cleared the corpus engagement floor.
content.caption: the median thing that works, before anyone tried anything

hypothesis: Pushing relatability above the corpus median should widen the audience that recognises itself in the post.

content.headline: when the syllabus says no extensions
content.visual_description: Static talking-head to camera, dorm room, overhead light. Text banner pinned top-third for the full run.
content.punchline: and the due date is during the career fair
content.caption: genuinely who approved this academic calendar

hypothesis: A POV frame makes the viewer a participant rather than an audience, which should raise the share rate.

content.headline: POV: you're the only one who did the reading
content.visual_description: Handheld POV walking into a seminar room. Slow pan across eleven closed laptops.
content.punchline: the professor makes eye contact. you are the seminar now.
content.caption: i will not be doing this again

hypothesis: Absurdist framing of an ordinary campus grievance should travel further than a sincere account of the same grievance.

content.headline: explaining my 4-hour gap between classes to my parents
content.visual_description: POV across a kitchen table. Subject gestures at a hand-drawn schedule taped to the wall as if briefing a war room.
content.punchline: "so from 11 to 3 I simply cease to exist"
content.caption: the gap is load-bearing

hypothesis: A sincere day-in-the-life may build a stronger parasocial bond and convert to follows even if it shares less.

content.headline: day in my life as a pre-med
content.visual_description: Morning-to-night vlog. Six a.m. alarm, library, cadaver lab exterior, 1am walk home.
content.punchline: (there is no punchline. that is the point.)
content.caption: romanticising it because the alternative is thinking about it

hypothesis: If absurdity is the active ingredient, more of it inside a longer mockumentary frame should compound the effect.

content.headline: the 4-hour gap, but it is a nature documentary
content.visual_description: Handheld long-lens shots of a student asleep across three library chairs. Whispered narration over the top.
content.punchline: "the specimen has selected its nesting site. it will not move until 3pm."
content.caption: observed in its natural habitat

hypothesis: Increasing absurdity while cutting time-to-punchline to under eight seconds should raise the share rate, because a meme has to be re-tellable before it can be re-posted.

content.headline: when you said one quick LeetCode problem
content.visual_description: Hard cut from a lit desk at 7pm to the same desk at 4am, same posture, forty-one browser tabs, sun coming up behind the blinds.
content.punchline: the problem was rated EASY
content.caption: see you tomorrow

hypothesis: Rendering the joke as a readable group chat should raise saves, because text is re-readable in a way that performance is not.

content.headline: the group chat at 3am before the deadline
content.visual_description: Screen recording of a five-person thread. Typing indicators start and stop. Nobody sends anything for nine seconds.
content.punchline: "has anyone started" (4 likes)
content.caption: we are a team

hypothesis: A deadpan explainer register lets the absurdity land without being announced, which should read as wittier and travel through quote-shares.

content.headline: library seat ownership law, explained
content.visual_description: Whiteboard diagram with legal citations to statutes that do not exist. Laser pointer. Absolutely straight face.
content.punchline: a water bottle establishes possession for ninety minutes. a laptop charger is adverse possession.
content.caption: precedent is precedent

hypothesis: If the winning structure is the structure and not the subject, transplanting it onto an unrelated topic should hold most of its fitness.

content.headline: when you said one quick gym session
content.visual_description: Same hard-cut structure as exp_006. 6pm lit gym, 9pm empty gym, identical posture on the same bench.
content.punchline: it was leg day. it is still leg day.
content.caption: see you tomorrow

hypothesis: Borrowing the speedrun frame imports an entire existing grammar — timer, split, category name — so the viewer already knows how to read the joke and can re-tell it in four words.

content.headline: the 11:59pm submission speedrun, any%
content.visual_description: Split-screen with a live millisecond timer. Green split text pops on every completed step. Final upload confirmation at 23:59:47.
content.punchline: NEW PERSONAL BEST — 13 seconds remaining
content.caption: any% no-sleep category

hypothesis: Opening mid-sentence with no setup should cut the scroll-past window to almost nothing.

content.headline: when the TA says 'this will be on the exam'
content.visual_description: Opens already mid-panic. Forty students turning to the same page in unison, filmed from the back row.
content.punchline: she said it about slide 4 of 212
content.caption: the whole room heard it

hypothesis: The historical corpus scores irony highly, so maximising it on top of the winning structure should be the single largest available gain.

content.headline: a deeply ironic meditation on the attendance policy
content.visual_description: Slow push-in on an empty lecture hall. Layered irony: the video is about not attending, filmed by someone attending.
content.punchline: the policy is the performance and we are all complicit, etc.
content.caption: anyway

hypothesis: Widening the topic from one major to the whole campus should grow the addressable audience without touching the structure that is working.

content.headline: the 8am lecture speedrun, glitchless
content.visual_description: Timer starts at the alarm. Splits for teeth, bus, coffee, door. Runner arrives as the slide deck opens.
content.punchline: GLITCHLESS — showered, technically
content.caption: glitchless category is harder

hypothesis: Pointing the speedrun frame at a shared institutional enemy rather than a personal habit should let the joke be re-told by people it did not happen to.

content.headline: financial aid portal speedrun (world record attempt)
content.visual_description: Cold open on a 2003-era portal already mid-session. Timer running. Two password resets, one PDF that opens in a new tab and immediately expires.
content.punchline: RUN VOIDED — session timed out at 4:51
content.caption: attempt 6

hypothesis: Dining hall content has the widest possible campus overlap, so the same structure should reach more people per share.

content.headline: the dining hall swipe speedrun
content.visual_description: Timer from door to table. Split for the omelette line. Runner loses eleven seconds to a friend who wants to catch up.
content.punchline: SOCIAL PENALTY — +11s
content.caption: the line is RNG

hypothesis: A four-player co-op framing needs more seconds to establish, and the payoff should justify the extra length.

content.headline: group project speedrun, 4 players
content.visual_description: Four-way split screen. Three panels idle for the entire run. One panel does everything.
content.punchline: CO-OP RUN — 1 player active
content.caption: i did not consent to this category

hypothesis: Holding the winning genome nearly fixed gives a clean control against which the three mutated siblings can be read.

content.headline: the parking permit speedrun
content.visual_description: Cold open on a permit queue at 6:40am. Timer. Runner reaches the window as the lot fills.
content.punchline: RUN FAILED — lot full at 6:52
content.caption: attempt 3

hypothesis: The housing lottery is the single most widely shared institutional grievance on campus, and framing it as RNG manipulation gives strangers a reason to send it to each other rather than merely recognise it.

content.headline: housing lottery speedrun (RNG manipulation)
content.visual_description: Cold open on a countdown already at 00:04. Lottery number reveal. Runner attempts four documented RNG-manipulation strategies, all superstition.
content.punchline: SEED WAS SET AT BIRTH
content.caption: rng is rigged

hypothesis: An exploration probe. Both the deadpan register and original audio were pruned in earlier generations, but never together and never on top of the speedrun frame — the agent has low confidence here and wants the measurement.

content.headline: course registration speedrun, co-op run
content.visual_description: Two roommates, two laptops, one shared schedule. Deadpan narration of a plan that survives four seconds of contact with the registrar.
content.punchline: DESYNC — both runners in the same section
content.caption: we practised this for a week
content.audio: original audio — keyboard, two people not talking

hypothesis: Awaiting a fitness estimate from the historical model.

content.headline: office hours speedrun
content.visual_description: Cold open on a corridor queue. Timer. Eleven minutes of waiting compressed to three seconds.
content.punchline: BOSS NOT SPAWNED — door locked, sign says back in 5
content.caption: attempt 2
